title: How to measure blood pressure at home
what: A monitor with an upper-arm cuff shows your blood pressure and pulse. Measuring the right way matters, or the numbers will be wrong.
why: For high blood pressure, adjusting treatment, heart or kidney disease, or pregnancy, as your doctor advises.
tell_doctor: Your home readings in the morning and evening
If your blood pressure jumps around a lot
If your monitor is a wrist one, not an upper-arm one

prepare.title: 30 minutes before
prepare.text: No smoking, no coffee or strong tea, and no exercise.

prepare.title: Before measuring
prepare.text: Use the toilet and sit quietly for 5 minutes.

prepare.title: Cuff
prepare.text: The cuff size must fit your arm. A cuff that is too small gives readings that are too high.

bring: Your blood pressure log. Show it to your doctor
steps: Sit on a chair with your back supported and feet flat on the floor. Do not cross your legs
Put the cuff on your bare upper arm, 2 to 3 cm (about 1 inch) above the elbow
Rest your arm on a table, with the cuff at heart level
Press the button. Do not talk or move
Write down both results and the time
feel: The cuff squeezes your arm tightly for a few seconds. That is normal
after: Usually you measure morning and evening for several days in a row. Your doctor will say how many
Do not change your medicine doses based on one reading. Show your log to your doctor
red_flags: Very high blood pressure with a headache, chest pain, trouble speaking, or weakness in an arm: call emergency services

faq.a: The first time, use both. After that, use the arm that gave the higher reading.

faq.q: Why is my blood pressure higher at the doctor's than at home?
faq.a: Nerves often raise blood pressure at the doctor's office. That is why a home log is so useful.

reminders.text: Time to check your blood pressure. Sit quietly for 5 minutes, cuff at heart level, and take two readings.
